0.0.n: という introduces the situation being summed up in the expression ということで.

0.1.n: こと turns the preceding idea into a thing or situation that can be discussed.

0.2.n: で marks the preceding situation as the basis for moving on to the next point.

0.4.n: こちら politely points to what the speaker is showing.

1.0.n: ホント is a casual spelling of 本当, often used for emphasis.

1.1.n: に combines with ホント to make ホントに, emphasizing that the speaker is serious.

2.0.n: 全 means all, and 財産 means assets; whose assets they are is understood from context.

3.0.n: 万 means ten thousand, so １万円 is one unit of ten thousand yen.

3.1.n: です gives the statement a polite ending.

4.0.n: これ stands alone to refer to the money the speaker has just shown.

4.1.n: を marks the money as what will be bet, though the verb comes later.

4.2.n: です is part of the conversational filler ですね here, not a completed statement.

4.3.n: ね keeps the listener engaged while the speaker pauses before continuing.

4.5.n: こちら shifts attention to the race the speaker is about to identify.

5.0.n: Before レース, this number identifies the race's position in the schedule.

5.1.n: レース is borrowed from English; 10レース here means race number ten.

5.2.m: linking race ten to its name
5.2.n: の connects the race number to the title that follows.

5.3.n: 神無月 is part of the race's name and is also a traditional Japanese name for October.

5.4.n: 特別 is part of the race title here, rather than an ordinary description.

5.5.n: です politely identifies the race by its title.

5.6.n: ね adds a conversational sense of checking or sharing the identification with the listener.

6.0.n: こちら refers back to the race just identified.

6.1.n: の connects こちら to 方 in the pointing expression こちらの方.

6.2.n: 方 makes the reference less direct; it does not refer to a person here.

6.3.n: の links the pointing expression こちらの方 to レース.

6.4.n: レース refers to the event on which the speaker intends to bet.

6.5.n: に marks the race as the target of the betting action.

7.0.n: この must come before a noun, here １万円.

7.1.n: The amount is repeated to emphasize exactly how much money will be wagered.

7.2.n: を identifies the amount being wagered as the object of 賭ける.

7.3.n: 一点張り means concentrating the wager on one selection, not necessarily a single horse.

7.4.n: で marks the betting method: concentrating everything on one selection.

8.0.n: 賭けたい is 賭ける with たい, expressing the speaker's desire to place a wager.

8.1.n: と marks 賭けたい as the thought expressed by 思います.

8.2.n: 思います is the polite form of 思う; after たいと, it softens a statement of intention.

0.lit: With that being the situation, this here.
0.tip: ということで is a common transition meaning so or with that said.

1.tip: ホントに can stand alone to stress sincerity or amazement.

2.tip: Japanese often leaves out my when ownership is clear from context.

3.tip: 万 counts in units of ten thousand, so １万円 is 10,000 yen.

4.tip: The を-marked object can appear well before its verb, with pauses and other phrases in between.

5.lit: Race ten's Kannazuki Special, it is, right.
5.tip: 神無月特別 is the race title, while 10レース identifies its number on the schedule.

6.lit: On the race of this one here…
6.tip: に marks what the bet targets; the betting verb arrives later.

7.lit: This 10,000 yen, by a single-selection bet…
7.tip: 一点張り means putting everything on one selection; it does not specify the type of horse-racing bet.

8.lit: I think that I want to bet.
8.tip: たいと思います commonly announces an intention gently, rather than expressing uncertainty.
